title: occupational hearing threshold shift guide
instruction:
You are Camila Bonneau, occupational health nurse supporting Ballantry Foundry, and Nikolai Ingram needs this before Friday’s review of the fourteen standard threshold shifts reported from the deboning lines. He has never handled a hearing case, and people are using “standard threshold shift” to mean both a clinical change and an OSHA-recordable case. A second problem is that the usual “ten-decibel loss means recordable” shortcut is being repeated even though age correction, the baseline, and two ambiguous cases make it unsafe here. Prepare a plain-language guide for Nikolai, using federal OSHA requirements current on December 31, 2024, so he can classify cases and understand the employer’s required follow-up without asking you what each term means. Cover the decision points, the 30-day retest window, age correction, baseline revision, recordkeeping, worker notification, hearing protection, and when exposure or medical follow-up matters; distinguish requirements from practical cautions and do not invent worker-specific results that were not provided. Keep it to two pages, avoid clinical diagnosis and names or identifiers, and make the same figures and definitions appear in both `hearing_threshold_shift_guide.docx` and `hearing_threshold_shift_guide.pdf`. Write both files into the top level of the working directory, using exactly those filenames. Sheafield Systems will circulate the PDF, while HR will retain the editable Word file.

---

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `hearing_threshold_shift_guide.docx` — A plain-language, audience-specific guide for the HR director explaining OSHA hearing threshold-shift recordability and employer follow-up duties. (Must be no more than two pages when rendered.; Must use fictional case identifiers only and omit employee names and direct identifiers.; Must state federal OSHA requirements current on December 31, 2024.; Must not invent results for the fourteen workers or claim that any particular worker is recordable without supplied audiogram data.; Must agree with the PDF on every shared definition, threshold, time period, and figure.)
- `hearing_threshold_shift_guide.pdf` — The circulation-ready PDF version of the same plain-language guide. (Must be no more than two pages when rendered.; Must be substantively and numerically identical to the DOCX.; Must use fictional case identifiers only and omit employee names and direct identifiers.; Must remain readable for an executive who has not handled a hearing case before.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

Hearing Threshold Shifts: HR Classification & Follow-up Guide
For the fourteen reported shifts from the deboning lines: classify only after reviewing the audiograms. No worker-level outcome can be decided from the count of reported shifts alone.
1. STS A standard threshold shift (STS) is a comparison result—not automatically a recordable case.
2. Recordability A separate OSHA recordkeeping decision with additional conditions.
3. Follow-up Hearing conservation duties can apply even when the 300 Log does not.
Key terms in plain language
Baseline 
the audiogram against which later thresholds are compared. Verify the correct worker, ear, date, and applicable prior audiogram before calculating any shift.
STS 
for each ear separately, an average worsening of 10 dB or more at 2,000, 3,000, and 4,000 Hz compared with the baseline. Either ear can meet the rule; both ears do not have to.
Recordable hearing-loss case 
a work-related, persistent/permanent STS that also shows an average total hearing level of 25 dB or more above audiometric zero at 2,000, 3,000, and 4,000 Hz in the same ear.
Decision sequence — use this order
1  VERIFY  Match the worker, ear, test date, baseline, and applicable prior audiogram; check that the comparison is usable.
2  CALCULATE  For each ear, average the change at 2/3/4 kHz. Is worsening 10 dB or more? If yes, it is an STS.
3  CONFIRM  The employer may retest within 30 days of the initial audiogram. Use the retest to determine whether the shift is confirmed; do not treat the initial result as final while that permitted window is being assessed.
4  RECORD?  For a final case, check separately: work-relatedness; persistence/permanence (not returned to baseline in the applicable assessment); and average total hearing level 25 dB or more above audiometric zero in the same ear. Record only when all apply.
5  ACT  Complete worker notice and hearing-conservation follow-up for an STS; complete OSHA recordkeeping only for a qualifying recordable case.
REQUIREMENT — age correction. For OSHA recordkeeping, the employer may use the age-correction tables in 29 CFR 1910.95 Appendix F when determining whether the recordability criteria are met. It is a limited permitted consideration—not a universal subtraction, not a substitute for the baseline comparison, and not a reason to skip the separate STS, 25 dB, work-relatedness, and persistence checks.


Employer Duties, Quality Checks & Safe Escalation
Use the labels below deliberately: REQUIREMENT = federal OSHA duty; CAUTION = do not make a premature classification; REVIEW = occupational-health/audiology assessment.
Required actions after the determination
STS notice 
REQUIREMENT — Notify the employee in writing within 21 days after the STS is determined. Inform the employee of the result and the need for hearing-protection/hearing-conservation follow-up as applicable.
Protection 
REQUIREMENT — When hearing-conservation requirements apply, provide and make hearing protectors available. Fit, refit, training, and actual use matter; handing over earplugs alone is not enough.
Exposure 
REQUIREMENT — Include employees exposed at or above an 85 dBA 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA) in the hearing conservation program. REVIEW — revisit exposure assessment and controls when shifts or conditions suggest a problem.
OSHA log 
REQUIREMENT — Enter a qualifying recordable case on the OSHA Form 300 Log within 7 calendar days after the case is determined. An STS by itself is not an automatic log entry.
Records 
REQUIREMENT — Retain audiometric records and supporting documentation under OSHA retention rules. Audiometric test records are retained for the affected employee’s employment; employee medical records are retained for employment plus 30 years where 29 CFR 1910.1020 applies.
Do not let the baseline or test quality decide the case by convenience
REQUIREMENT — baseline revision. Do not revise a baseline merely to make a shift disappear. An annual audiogram may replace the baseline only when the audiologist, otolaryngologist, or physician determines that the STS is persistent; use another revision basis only if the governing requirement permits it.
CAUTION — quality first. Inadequate quiet before testing, poor test conditions/equipment, or a temporary conductive issue can distort a comparison. Do not treat that result as settled; arrange review or permitted retesting before final classification.
REVIEW — professional follow-up. Seek occupational-health or audiology review for questionable test quality, a possible temporary medical condition, persistent shift, referral criteria, or uncertainty about work-relatedness. Threshold data do not diagnose a condition or establish benefits.
Two generic ambiguity reminders (not findings for any worker)
Case A 
A 10 dB STS can exist but still fail the separate 25 dB hearing-level-above-audiometric-zero criterion; it is not automatically recordable.
Case B 
A questionable initial result may require quality review or the permitted 30-day retest; it is not automatically confirmed or erased.
Classification-and-duty summary
For each reported shift: verify the record and test quality; calculate STS ear-by-ear; consider the 30-day retest; then make the distinct recordability decision using the 25 dB criterion, work-relatedness, and persistence/permanence. Give timely written STS notice and protection/program follow-up as applicable. Log only a qualifying case. Send unresolved facts to occupational health/audiology—do not assign a worker-specific result without the audiogram and review.
Authority snapshot: 29 CFR 1904.10; 29 CFR 1910.95(g), (i), (m) and Appendix F; 29 CFR 1910.1020. Federal OSHA framework current as of December 31, 2024.

spec.professional_context: This is an occupational-health communication package for an enterprise food-manufacturing employer. The reader is an HR director who needs accurate, self-contained explanations of recordability and follow-up duties, not a clinical diagnosis or a recommendation about individual employees.
difficulty_sources: Distinguishing standard threshold shift from an OSHA-recordable hearing-loss case
Applying age correction, baseline comparison, and the 30-day retest window without collapsing them into one shortcut
Explaining employer duties in plain language for a non-clinical executive
Keeping a DOCX and PDF version numerically and substantively aligned

authoring_plan.purpose: Construct an offline gold package consisting of a two-page plain-language hearing-threshold-shift guide in DOCX and an equivalent PDF. The files should be authored from federal OSHA occupational knowledge current through December 31, 2024, not from supplied reference files.
content_constraints: Use a short executive-facing explanation followed by a compact decision aid.
Keep STS, recordability, work-relatedness, permanence, retesting, and hearing-conservation duties visibly distinct.

Include the exact professional thresholds and periods scored in the rubric: 10 dB average at 2/3/4 kHz, 25 dB above audiometric zero, 30-day retest, 7-calendar-day log deadline, 21-day written notice, 85 dBA 8-hour TWA, and 30-year medical-record retention where applicable.
Explain age correction as a limited recordability consideration, not a universal subtraction and not a replacement for the STS calculation.
Explain baseline verification and permitted revision cautiously; prohibit changing a baseline simply to remove an inconvenient shift.
Include audiogram-quality and temporary-condition cautions, plus a clear boundary against diagnosing or deciding unprovided worker-specific cases.
Use generic fictional labels such as Case A and Case B only if examples are needed; do not create actual employee results.
Minimize sensitive content and avoid employee names, identifiers, or unnecessary audiometric data.

gold_derivation.definitions: Build a terminology block defining baseline, STS, recordable hearing-loss case, age correction, permanence, and work-relatedness.
gold_derivation.decision_logic: Derive the flow from record verification and test quality through frequency-specific average, STS determination, 25 dB criterion, age correction where permitted, work-relatedness/permanence review, and final recordkeeping decision.
gold_derivation.follow_up: Derive a separate duty block covering written employee notification within 21 days, OSHA 300-log entry within 7 calendar days after determination, hearing protection and conservation-program implications, exposure review at 85 dBA 8-hour TWA, and professional follow-up.
gold_derivation.ambiguity_handling: Include two clearly labeled generic ambiguous examples: one where the 10 dB shift does not satisfy the additional recordability condition, and one where retesting or quality review prevents an immediate final classification. Do not assign either example to the fourteen actual workers.
gold_derivation.cross_file_validation: Generate the PDF from the finalized DOCX or compare extracted text after conversion; verify that every shared number, definition, and duty remains identical.

review_checks: Render both files and confirm no more than two pages.
Check that all rubric thresholds and deadlines are present and accurately qualified.
Check that no claim says every STS is recordable or that age correction automatically removes a case.
Check that the final summary is actionable for classification and escalation but contains no worker-specific verdict.
Check DOCX/PDF substantive equivalence and absence of sensitive identifiers.

deliverables.description: A plain-language, audience-specific guide for the HR director explaining OSHA hearing threshold-shift recordability and employer follow-up duties.
constraints: Must be no more than two pages when rendered.
Must use fictional case identifiers only and omit employee names and direct identifiers.
Must state federal OSHA requirements current on December 31, 2024.
Must not invent results for the fourteen workers or claim that any particular worker is recordable without supplied audiogram data.
Must agree with the PDF on every shared definition, threshold, time period, and figure.

deliverables.description: The circulation-ready PDF version of the same plain-language guide.
constraints: Must be no more than two pages when rendered.
Must be substantively and numerically identical to the DOCX.
Must use fictional case identifiers only and omit employee names and direct identifiers.
Must remain readable for an executive who has not handled a hearing case before.
